result:
I made a one-line-logic change in `mitmproxy/addons/next_layer.py` (`_get_client_hello`). I haven't run it or the tests, and I haven't confirmed this is the cause of the stall.

**Suspected cause:** When a QUIC ClientHello isn't complete yet, `quic_parse_client_hello_from_datagrams` returns `None`. This happens when the hello spans several datagrams, as with Chrome's larger hellos. `_get_client_hello` treated that `None` as "no ClientHello here". The ignore check then had no SNI to match against `ignore_hosts`, so it decided "not ignored". The connection was then handed to the QUIC interception layers instead of being passed through.

**Fix:** For UDP, an incomplete QUIC hello now raises `NeedsMoreData`, the same as the existing DTLS and TCP-TLS branches. The layer decision is deferred until the rest of the hello arrives, and the ignore/allow check then sees the SNI.

**Tests:** I didn't add one. I tried a case with a truncated `quic_client_hello`, but a cut-off encrypted packet most likely fails decryption and gives `ValueError`, not `None`. So that test wouldn't have exercised the new branch, and I removed it. A proper test needs a hello split across two real datagrams.
